parts.note: to beg is to request earnestly
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone opens by asking about a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: Began is the past tense of begin, a synonym of started.

clue.text: Graduate's to go round Caribbean island

indicators.note: the words to go are placed round the graduate's letters, enclosing them

parts.note: taken as written
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A new graduate is about to tour a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is the smaller island of the nation Trinidad and Tobago in the West Indies.

indicators.note: something ripped is torn apart, so the letters of veil once are rearranged

explanation.surface: A veil, once torn off by force.
explanation.definitionFit: Violence is the use of physical force to harm.

explanation.surface: A business doing badly leaves everyone baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading at a loss means without profit; being at a loss also means baffled or unsure what to do.

clue.text: A very hot day for one reckoning to install central heating

indicators.note: to install something is to put it in place inside, so CH goes inside the other word

parts.note: a scorer is one who reckons up the points
CH is the usual abbreviation for central heating, seen in house adverts

explanation.surface: On a sweltering day, an accountant wants central heating fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorcher is informal for a day of blazing heat.

explanation.surface: A boat carrying nuclear missiles.
explanation.walkthrough: Britannia was the British royal yacht; Britannia is also the female figure personifying Britain, shown holding a trident. Trident is also Britain's nuclear missile system, the misleading surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Yacht bore that name, and the national emblem on old British pennies carries a three-pronged spear.

explanation.surface: Someone gets cash in exchange for a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: To negotiate a cheque is to exchange it for cash; to negotiate is also to treat, as in deal or bargain with someone.

parts.note: a child in your charge is in your care

explanation.surface: A second accusation alarms someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To scare is to make someone afraid.

clue.text: Bird that sounds what's needed for the rotisserie

indicators.note: the bird's name, spoken, sounds like the kitchen item

parts.note: meat on a rotisserie is held on a skewer

explanation.surface: A bird that is perfect for roasting on a spit.
explanation.definitionFit: A skua is a predatory seabird.

clue.text: Corresponding, but never going to meet?

explanation.surface: Two things match, yet will never come together.
explanation.walkthrough: Parallel lines run side by side for ever without meeting, the cryptic second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel means similar or matching, and parallel lines keep the same distance apart and so never cross.

clue.text: Sport where one is liable to get the chop

definitions.text: Sport where one is liable to get the chop

parts.words: Sport where one is liable to get the chop
parts.note: to get the chop means to be sacked, but here a martial art uses hand chops

explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese martial art is famous for its chopping blows with the side of the hand.

explanation.surface: Urging an idiot to carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on is to carry on; a goon is a silly or stupid person.

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the singing word swallows the potatoes

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
mash is mashed potato

explanation.surface: A woman named Carol tucks into mashed potato and loves it.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is British informal for excellent or terrific.

clue.text: It's only a bit of water

explanation.surface: Something dismissed as just a puddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than; a mere is also a lake or pond, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Vital to add good score to total

parts.note: par is the standard good score in golf
an amount is a total or sum

explanation.surface: It is essential to add a good score to the running total.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme or of chief importance.

explanation.surface: A burglar is studied during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: To case a joint is criminal slang for checking out a place before robbing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar inspects premises beforehand; a legal action heard in court is a lawsuit.

clue.text: By and by-no one knows who by

explanation.surface: Soon we will learn the writer's identity is a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon, and the abbreviation for anonymous marks a work whose author is unknown.

clue.text: Near the eruption of the ground

indicators.note: an eruption throws things about, so the letters of near the are scrambled

explanation.surface: A volcanic eruption close to the earth's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen means made of earth or soil.

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge and begins to bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls; a new bowler takes over at the end of one.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume control of something is to take charge; in cricket, a bowler starting the next set of six balls does so.

explanation.surface: A criminal raid to rustle livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: A ram raid is a British term for driving a vehicle through a shop window to loot it; read literally it is a raid on male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash-and-grab using a car as battering ram; humorously, a theft of rams, which are male sheep.

clue.text: You have a direct line, but can't speak, to him

definitions.text: You have a direct line, but can't speak, to him

parts.words: You have a direct line, but can't speak, to him
parts.note: a direct line suggests a phone, but means lineage from a forebear who is long dead

explanation.definitionFit: A forebear from whom you descend in a direct line, usually dead and so beyond conversation.

parts.note: O is the zero shape, nothing
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A man named Frank has nothing to write about.
explanation.definitionFit: Open means candid, honest and forthright.

parts.note: reads as a polar ruler, but the emperor is a species of large flightless bird living there

explanation.definitionFit: The emperor is the largest species of this flightless seabird, breeding on Antarctic ice.

clue.text: In London thoroughfare, stop car and lean out

parts.note: to park is to stop and leave a car

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of lean are rearranged

explanation.surface: On a London street, a driver pulls over and leans out of the window.
explanation.walkthrough: PARK LANE is a famous upmarket road in London's Mayfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy street on the east side of Hyde Park, famous from the Monopoly board.

explanation.surface: Trimming lines from a sheet of graph paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Axes means chops or cuts; it is also the plural of axis, the reference lines of a chart.

explanation.surface: Getting ready to shoot a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To cock a gun is to raise its hammer ready to fire; a cock is a male bird.

clue.text: Rough place for golf, it's said

parts.note: golf is played on a course

explanation.surface: The golf venue is reportedly rough terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means crude or rough in texture.

indicators.note: get here means become, so the letters of mitre may become something new

explanation.surface: Virtue may earn a bishop his mitre.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence, the good qualities that deserve reward.

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, an army doctor
someone promoted rose in rank

explanation.surface: A downcast military doctor gets a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and ill-tempered.

clue.text: Some rags may be made of fine material

indicators.note: the letters of some rags may be made into a new word by rearranging

explanation.surface: Old rags can be turned into delicate fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is a very thin, light gauze or cobweb-like fabric.

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the words orange liqueur, used within them

explanation.surface: Ingredients in an orange liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a heavenly spirit.

clue.text: Diamonds, for example, look good on young girl

indicators.note: in an across clue on puts the second piece after the first

parts.note: a minor is a young person under the age of majority
clothes that suit you look good on you

explanation.surface: Diamond jewellery looks good on a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, diamonds and clubs are the lower-ranking suits.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, diamonds is one of the two lower-ranking card suits, along with clubs.
